skill.name: git-commit
skill.description: Create standardized git commits by analyzing diffs, selecting conventional commit types, staging relevant files, and generating clear commit messages.
skill.summary: Analyze repository changes and create conventional git commits with safe staging guidance.
skill.author: github

security_audit.summary: Static analysis primarily matched Markdown fences, inline conventional commit examples, and documented git commands. I found no evidence of malicious execution, prompt injection, network access, credential exfiltration, or secret harvesting in SKILL.md.

remediation.issue: The skill relies on Bash for git operations.
remediation.suggestion: Keep the existing safety protocol and require explicit user approval before destructive git commands, force pushes, or hook bypasses.

remediation.issue: The staging examples include broad patterns such as wildcard file selection.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer staging explicit file paths when possible, and inspect git status before committing to avoid including unrelated files.

content.value_statement: Writing clear commit messages takes time and can be inconsistent across teams. This skill analyzes your diff and guides Claude, Codex, or Claude Code to create focused conventional commits.
actual_capabilities: Inspects staged and unstaged git changes before creating a commit.
Selects a conventional commit type such as feat, fix, docs, test, or chore.
Suggests a scope and concise imperative description from the diff.
Guides logical staging of files when no files are already staged.
Creates single-line or multi-line commit messages with optional body and footer.
Applies safety rules for secrets, hooks, force pushes, and destructive git commands.
limitations: Requires Bash access because it depends on local git commands.
Does not verify remote repository policy or branch protection settings.
May need user judgment when a diff contains several unrelated changes.
Cannot guarantee that broad staging patterns exclude every sensitive or unrelated file.

use_cases.title: Commit a focused feature change
use_cases.description: Turn a completed feature diff into a conventional commit with a clear type, scope, and concise message.

use_cases.title: Standardize team commit history
use_cases.description: Use consistent commit types and formatting so changelog tools and reviewers can understand changes quickly.

use_cases.title: Prepare safe commits during code review
use_cases.description: Review status, avoid secrets, and group staged files before committing review fixes.

prompt_templates.title: Create a simple commit
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a conventional git commit for my current changes. Check what changed, suggest the message, and commit only the relevant files.

prompt_templates.title: Commit only staged files
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when the user already staged a logical change.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use only the staged changes to create a conventional commit. Do not stage any other files.

prompt_templates.title: Split mixed changes
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when the diff contains unrelated work.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my working tree and recommend how to split it into logical conventional commits. Start with the first safe commit only.

prompt_templates.title: Create a commit with body and footer
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow for complex changes or issue references.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a conventional commit with a concise subject, a short body explaining the reason, and any issue references from the change context.

output_examples.output: The assistant reviews the staged diff, identifies it as a fix, creates a concise conventional commit message, and reports the new commit hash.

output_examples.input: My working tree has docs and test changes. Help me commit them cleanly.
output_examples.output: The assistant separates the changes by purpose, recommends committing the documentation update first, stages the selected files, and creates a focused commit.

output_examples.input: Create a commit for this breaking configuration change.
output_examples.output: The assistant prepares a conventional commit that marks the breaking change and includes a short footer explaining the compatibility impact.

best_practices: Review git status and diff before allowing the skill to commit changes.
Commit one logical change at a time for clear review and rollback history.
Use explicit file paths for staging when sensitive or unrelated files may be present.
anti_patterns: Do not use broad staging patterns when the working tree contains secrets or generated files.
Do not bypass commit hooks unless the user explicitly requests it and accepts the risk.
Do not combine unrelated features, fixes, and formatting changes in one commit.

faq.question: Does this skill create commits automatically?
faq.answer: It can create commits through git commands when the user asks for a commit and grants the required tool access.

faq.question: Does it follow Conventional Commits?
faq.answer: Yes. It uses conventional types such as feat, fix, docs, test, refactor, chore, and related formats.

faq.question: Can it stage files for me?
faq.answer: Yes. It can stage specific files or recommend logical groups, but users should review status before committing.

faq.question: Will it commit secrets?
faq.answer: The skill warns against committing secrets and recommends checking for .env files, credentials, and private keys.

faq.question: Can it handle breaking changes?
faq.answer: Yes. It supports conventional breaking-change markers and footers when the diff indicates a compatibility impact.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code when they have appropriate local git access.
